text.title: Laravel Layered Architecture Examples
text.summary: Worked example: migrating a 612-line fat OrderController to the Controller → Service → Resource layering, driven by an audit that must reach zero.

example.context: Laravel 11 commerce app. `OrderController.php` is 612 lines across 8 methods, each 70-90 lines with inline `validate()`, a controller-level `DB::transaction`, a raw model return and an inline `abort(403)` check.
example.walk: Step 1: run `scripts/laravel-anti-pattern-lint.sh` — 8 fat methods, 8 inline validations, 8 raw responses, 8 inline authorization checks, 6 controller-level transactions. Step 2: extract `OrderService` with create / update / cancel / ship / refund methods, each wrapping its writes in `DB::transaction(fn() => ...)`. Step 3: generate `StoreOrderRequest`, `UpdateOrderRequest`, `CancelOrderRequest`, moving rules and messages out of the controller. Step 4: `OrderResource` with an explicit field list; `OrderPolicy` covering create / update / cancel / refund, registered in `AuthServiceProvider` and reached via `authorizeResource` in the constructor. Step 5: re-run the audit — zero violations — and record the layering rules in `CONTRIBUTING.md` plus the PR template.
example.output: `OrderController` drops to ~120 lines (8 methods averaging 15 lines); business logic is unit-testable without HTTP; authorization is centralised; every new endpoint inherits the shape.

list.item: Any controller method over 20 lines → extract a service method (`thin-controller-no-eloquent`).
`DB::transaction` inside a controller → move it into the service (`db-transaction-closure`).
`return $model;` from a controller → wrap in a JsonResource (`jsonresource-from-controller-only`).
